channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Manufacturing
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] Clop wrote a web shell just for PTC Windchill — and it hides inside the application’s own identity
item.description: ReliaQuest has published analysis of the Java/JSP web shell Clop deployed in its PTC Windchill and FlexPLM data-theft campaign, and it is not an off-the-shelf implant. It is written against Windchill’s internal APIs, database schema, keystore and file-vault layout, and it does four things: decrypt stored credentials, enumerate repositories, retrieve files in bulk, and execute arbitrary Java. The detection problem is the part worth taking to your SOC — because the implant runs under the application’s own service identity, database telemetry can read the theft as ordinary application behaviour. There is no encryption payload and no observed reach into plant-floor systems. The campaign now stands at 43-plus named victims, including Shell (Clop claims about 89 GB), GE, and Philips, which says the intrusion was contained with no customer-environment impact. The flaw is CVE-2026-12569; PTC began patching on 17 June and CISA added it to KEV on 25 June, but exploitation is assessed to have started weeks earlier. - ReliaQuest research and Clop leak-site listings — reported by BleepingComputer - Exploited from early Jun 2026; web shell analysis published 18 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] The Iranian PLC campaign now covers Siemens and Schneider controllers — and at one victim the safety logic was disabled
item.description: Joint advisory AA26-097A, issued 7 April by the FBI, CISA, NSA, EPA, DOE, US Cyber Command’s Cyber National Mission Force and Treasury and expanded on 22 July, describes Iranian-affiliated actors reaching internet-exposed programmable logic controllers across US critical infrastructure. Two points matter on a plant floor. The observed manufacturer scope has widened from Rockwell Automation to Schneider Electric and Siemens, which covers most of the installed base in discrete and process manufacturing. And at one confirmed US victim the actors modified ladder logic to disable safety shutdown and alarm functions, allowing unsafe conditions to develop without alerting operators — a different and more serious outcome than lockout. The agencies also documented project-file exfiltration and Dropbear SSH persistence. No CVE is involved; exposure and weak credentials are the way in. - CISA/FBI joint advisory AA26-097A — corroborated by SecurityWeek - Issued 7 Apr 2026, updated 22 Jul 2026; campaign ongoing through mid-Aug 2026

item.title: [High] Attackers crossed between two unrelated operators over a private cellular APN and stopped a turbine
item.description: CERT Polska has disclosed that attackers reached the control network of a Polish combined heat and power plant serving about 50,000 residents, stopping a steam turbine and the plant’s process-water treatment system. The path in was neither the internet nor the corporate network: a compromised FortiGate firewall at an unrelated wind farm, then a Teltonika cellular router that reached a private APN operated by the distribution system operator, on which devices could reach one another. CERT Polska believes this is the first observed real-world use of a private APN as a route into an industrial control network. Manufacturers should read it as a warning about shared bearers generally — the private APNs and machine-builder cellular links used for remote diagnostics on packaging, robotics and utility skids follow the same pattern. - CERT Polska disclosure — via Help Net Security and BleepingComputer - Incident Dec 2025; disclosed 8 Aug 2026, analysis published 11–13 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] CISA and the FBI now count more than 500 Medusa victims — and the group weaponises new flaws inside a day
item.description: The #StopRansomware advisory on Medusa, AA25-071A, was refreshed on 18 August. The cumulative victim tally passed 500 critical-infrastructure organisations as of April 2026, up from roughly 300 in the March 2025 version — about 200 new victims in a year. Critical manufacturing is named among the core target sectors, alongside healthcare, the defense industrial base, government facilities, IT and financial services. The operationally load-bearing finding is speed: Medusa has been observed weaponising newly disclosed vulnerabilities within roughly 24 hours, and in some cases using exploits up to a week before public disclosure, because it buys capability rather than developing it. Impact is enterprise-IT encryption plus data theft; no control-system involvement is alleged. For a plant that means the patch window normally negotiated with production is, against this actor, already closed. - CISA/FBI #StopRansomware advisory AA25-071A (updated) - Advisory refreshed 18 Aug 2026; victim tally current to Apr 2026

item.title: [High] Manufacturing took 747 of 1,140 industrial ransomware incidents in Q2 — 65 percent of the total
item.description: Dragos recorded 1,140 ransomware incidents against industrial organisations in the second quarter of 2026, up 12 percent from 1,020 in the first. Manufacturing absorbed 747 of them, about 65 percent. Construction accounted for 176, the engineering firms and system integrators that support control environments for 117, equipment manufacturing for 114 and food and beverage for 70. The United States alone recorded 431, 38 percent of the global total, and the most active claimants were Qilin with 140, Akira with 129 and The Gentlemen with 125. The finding worth carrying into a plant meeting is the negative one: across all 1,140 incidents Dragos identified zero cases in which an operator reached Stage 2 of the ICS Cyber Kill Chain, and zero cases of direct control-system manipulation. Where production stopped, it stopped because virtualisation or ERP was encrypted — not because anyone touched a controller. - Dragos Industrial Ransomware Analysis, Q2 2026 — via Help Net Security - Published 10 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] CISA added the exploited vCenter flaw to KEV yesterday — 361 hosts compromised across 47 countries
item.description: CISA added CVE-2026-59310, a path-traversal flaw in VMware vCenter Server, to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 18 August. Broadcom patched it on 29 July; exploitation began about five days later. German incident-response firm QUIRSO assesses with moderate confidence that a Chinese-speaking actor operates the campaign, counting roughly 361 affected addresses across 47 countries, with Germany, the United States, Turkey, Iran and France most represented. The actor gains root on the vCenter appliance, plants a backdoor via cron and a reverse SSH binary, and in at least one case deployed Babuk-derived ransomware. In most plants the historian, MES servers, SCADA nodes and engineering workstation images all live on one vSphere cluster — which makes the management plane a single point of compromise for the whole OT estate. - CISA KEV catalogue and QUIRSO research — via The Hacker News - Patched 29 Jul 2026; exploitation from early Aug; added to KEV 18 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] Gunra ransomware names critical manufacturing, and gets in through unpatched Fortinet devices
item.description: CISA, the FBI, NSA, DC3, the Secret Service and South Korea’s National Police Agency published #StopRansomware advisory AA26-222A on 10 August covering Gunra, a double-extortion operation derived from leaked Conti source code that moved to a ransomware-as-a-service affiliate model this year. Critical manufacturing and construction appear explicitly in the sector list, alongside transportation, utilities and government facilities. The initial access is unglamorous and therefore actionable: affiliates exploit CVE-2024-55591 and CVE-2025-24472 in internet-facing FortiOS and FortiProxy, long-patched authentication bypasses that grant super-admin and defeat multi-factor authentication. The advisory includes indicators and detection content, so this is a hunt that can be run this week. - CISA #StopRansomware advisory AA26-222A - Published 10 Aug 2026

item.title: [Medium] Thirty percent of UK manufacturers had a serious incident last year, and only half have a written recovery process
item.description: Make UK’s cyber security in manufacturing research, published this month, found that 30 percent of UK manufacturers suffered a serious cyber incident in the past year, directly or through their supply chain. The governance figures behind that number are the more useful part: only 51 percent hold an internal incident response and recovery process, 45 percent have a named senior owner for cyber, 23 percent have a CISO and 39 percent discuss it regularly at board level. Patch-management adoption sits at 36 percent. Separately, Bridewell reported that manufacturing accounts for roughly 40 percent of infostealer victims among UK critical national infrastructure organisations — harvested credentials being the commodity that feeds the extortion numbers elsewhere on this page. - Make UK cyber security in manufacturing report; Bridewell CNI research via Industrial Cyber - Published Aug 2026

item.title: [Critical] SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced exposes Node-RED with no authentication — maximum-severity remote code execution
item.description: Siemens ProductCERT advisory SSA-834709 covers CVE-2026-58115, rated CVSS 10.0 under both v3.1 and v4.0, in SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices running Industrial OS with Node-RED installed. The Node-RED HTTP interface enforces no authentication at all, so any remote unauthenticated attacker can create flows using programming nodes that execute system commands, giving arbitrary code execution at maximum privilege on the gateway. All versions before V4.3.4.1 are affected. Two things make it easy to miss: there is no corresponding CISA ICS advisory, so estates that track ICS-CERT rather than vendor PSIRT feeds will not see it; and IoT2050 gateways typically arrive in manufacturing as edge collectors and protocol converters feeding an OEE, historian or cloud analytics platform — devices the control network trusts, commissioned during a digitalisation project and then left out of the patch cycle entirely. - Siemens ProductCERT advisory SSA-834709 - Published 11 Aug 2026 (August ICS Patch Tuesday)

item.title: [Critical] A CVSS 10.0 command injection gives unauthenticated root on Haiwell’s IoT Cloud HMI gateway
item.description: CISA advisory ICSA-26-225-02 covers CVE-2026-19188, an OS command injection in the Haiwell IoT Cloud HMI Gateway rated 10.0. The Net Check feature reached through the /setting endpoint passes user input from the cmdPing Socket.io event to the operating system unsanitised, letting an unauthenticated remote attacker execute commands as root. Version 3.40.1.12 is affected; Haiwell has published Scada-v3.50.1.19. Low-cost HMI gateways of this type reach plants inside packaged machinery — a filler, a palletiser, a compressor skid, a chiller — specified by the machine builder rather than by your controls standard, which is why they rarely appear in an asset inventory until someone scans for them. - CISA ICS advisory ICSA-26-225-02 - Published 13 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] A Windows IKE flaw entered KEV on 18 August with a three-day deadline — and IKE is how vendors reach your plant
item.description: CISA added CVE-2026-33824, a double free in the Microsoft Windows IKE extensions service (IKEEXT) that allows remote code execution, to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 18 August with a federal remediation deadline of 21 August. A three-day deadline is a signal in itself; CISA reserves that compression for exploitation it assesses as widespread. The manufacturing relevance is the protocol rather than the product. IKE and IPsec terminate the site-to-site tunnels and vendor remote-access links that machine builders, systems integrators and corporate support use to reach plant networks, so a host running this service usually sits on a boundary that matters. Three further flaws were added the same day, including the VMware vCenter path traversal covered elsewhere on this page. - CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue - Added to KEV 18 Aug 2026; federal remediation due 21 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] Another wave of Siemens engineering-software parser bugs — Simcenter, Solid Edge and Parasolid all lose on opening a file
item.description: CISA advisory ICSA-26-230-02, published 18 August, covers CVE-2026-59086, a stack-based buffer overflow at CVSS 7.8 in Simcenter Nastran and Simcenter Femap that triggers when an affected binary is run with a malicious string as a file argument; V2606 fixes it. It extends a pattern set on 13 August. ICSA-26-225-12 lists seven memory-safety flaws in Solid Edge (CVE-2026-50058 through CVE-2026-50064, 7.8 each) in the DFT, PAR and PSM design-file parsers; ICSA-26-225-10 covers an out-of-bounds read in Parasolid (CVE-2026-64629); ICSA-26-225-11 covers two more in Simcenter Femap. Two others from that batch deserve separate attention: Siveillance Video (ICSA-26-225-09, CVE-2026-3014, CVSS 9.1) allows OS command injection through the Management Server API, and LOGO! Soft Comfort (ICSA-26-225-13) protects project files with a hardcoded AES key and unsalted SHA-256 password hashes — updating to V9 only removes the exposure if a LOGO! V9 hardware module or later is used with it. - CISA ICS advisories ICSA-26-230-02 and the 13 Aug Siemens batch (ICSA-26-225-09 to -13) - Published 13 and 18 Aug 2026

item.title: [Medium] Six flaws in CISA’s own Malcolm OT monitoring suite, including an 8.8 upload-to-code-execution
item.description: ICSA-26-230-01, published 18 August, discloses six vulnerabilities in Malcolm, CISA’s free open-source network traffic analysis suite for OT. The most serious is CVE-2026-55676 at CVSS 8.8, an unrestricted file upload that allows PHP to be uploaded and executed. The rest are a path traversal on archive extraction (CVE-2026-63177, 7.1), two authorisation bypasses via unnormalised URI paths and percent-encoding (CVE-2026-63134 and CVE-2026-19670, 5.4 each) and two further issues at 6.5, plus resource-exhaustion denial of service. Fixes land in Malcolm 26.07.0 and 26.08.0 depending on the CVE. What makes this worth reading is where the software sits: inside the OT network, usually fed by a SPAN or TAP with visibility across the plant. A compromised sensor is a map of the environment and a foothold in it. No exploitation is reported. - CISA ICS advisory ICSA-26-230-01 - Published 18 Aug 2026

item.title: [Low] The new National Security Science and Technology Strategy names OT and ICS resilience as a priority
item.description: The National Security Science and Technology Strategy, released on 19 August, sets out four pillars and names operational technology and industrial control system resilience, together with technology supply chains, as explicit priorities. For manufacturers the supply-chain framing has the longer reach: it covers the security of the components, software and equipment that arrive on the plant floor, not only the operator’s own network. Nothing changes for an operator today — this is a strategy document rather than a rule, and no reporting obligation or standard follows from it. It is a reasonable indicator of where federal attention is heading, and that has historically preceded procurement conditions and sector guidance. - National Security Science & Technology Strategy — via Industrial Cyber - Released 19 Aug 2026
